title: Which AION 2 class should you play?
description: Choose by the decisions you enjoy making, then compare your shortlist with a repeatable trial.
keywords: Start with your job, not a letter grade A useful first choice is the responsibility you want in a fight. Templars suit interest in the frontline, Clerics in healing, and Chanters in supporting a party. Damage-oriented choices then split into close-range and ranged styles. These are orientation labels drawn from class identities, not a ranking of current balance. A class can feel comfortable in one activity and demanding in another. Build a two-class shortlist Compare one familiar option with one that genuinely interests you. Gladiator versus Assassin asks whether you prefer sustained frontline involvement or precise engagements. Ranger versus Sorcerer asks whether physical ranged combat or a magic-focused sequence appeals more. Cleric versus Chanter is a question about primary responsibility, rather than which is universally better. Include Spiritmaster if summon management itself sounds enjoyable. Avoid levelling all eight just to postpone a decision. Use the same trial for both Give each candidate a short, comparable session. Use similar progression, equipment and the same available encounter; do not compare a geared main against a fresh alternate. Notice three things: whether you can see important threats, whether the controls feel comfortable, and whether you enjoy the recovery after a mistake. A clean repeated run is more informative than a highlight clip. Record what you disliked as well as what felt powerful. Match the class to your actual week If most sessions are short and solo, test solo comfort first. If you have a regular group, discuss missing responsibilities and schedules before rerolling. For PvP, identify whether you mean duels, small groups or larger fights; those contexts ask different questions. Do not treat an unlabelled PvP tier list as a universal answer. The comparison tool below deliberately uses roles and range rather than unsupported damage scores. What would change this recommendation? Revisit the choice when your preferred activity changes, when a patch substantially alters a mechanic you rely on, or when the controls continue to feel uncomfortable after practice. A small balance change is not by itself a reason to abandon a character. Before following a build from Korea, confirm the skill exists in your client and that its description matches. This guide is editorial decision support; it is not a tested endgame build.

title: Your first session: a plan that survives launch week
description: A practical order for settings, character choice and your first repeatable gameplay loop.
keywords: Check the service you are entering NC announced the global PC launch on October 5, 2026. Use the official site or Steam listing to reach the correct client for your region. An old test client, a Korean guide and the global release can describe different things. Before committing to a character, coordinate region, faction and server with anyone you intend to play with. Read the current selection screen and notice rather than assuming a later transfer will solve a mismatch. Make the game readable before making it fast Spend a few minutes on camera sensitivity, text size and the visibility of party information. Place your most frequently needed inputs where you can reach them while moving. Change one setting at a time and revisit it in the same scene. If a performance issue occurs only in crowds, compare the same crowded area rather than judging a change from an empty room. We do not prescribe a universal graphics preset or claim an FPS gain. Follow one progression thread For the first session, follow the game’s introductory progression until you understand movement, targeting and the menus it has actually unlocked. When a new system appears, read its cost and purpose before spending. Keep a short note of anything unclear and continue with a known objective. Opening every menu notification can consume the whole session without teaching you a useful combat loop. Delay choices you cannot explain Before opening a choice box or committing a scarce resource, ask what the item does, whether it is restricted to this character, and whether your next objective needs it. These are questions to answer from the current item text; this guide does not assume particular transfer or refund rules. There is little value in copying a veteran’s spending order when your own bottleneck is still learning an encounter. End with a next-session note Finish with one concrete objective: test a different keybind, practise a familiar encounter, or resolve a question about an unlocked system. Use the planner for your own tasks, not as a list of mandatory game dailies. It saves in this browser and has a manual reset, so no unverified regional reset time is silently applied. A small plan you return to is more useful than a long checklist you abandon.

title: How to use a Korean guide on global servers
description: A four-part compatibility check before copying a rotation, build or spending recommendation.
keywords: Keep four labels beside every recommendation Write down region, date, activity and assumptions. Region tells you which service was observed. Date tells you whether later changes may matter. Activity distinguishes solo progression, group PvE and different kinds of PvP. Assumptions include equipment, unlocked systems and party support. A recommendation with none of those labels may still contain a useful idea, but it is a poor instruction to copy exactly. Translate the mechanic, not just the sentence Keep the Korean skill or item name alongside the proposed English name until you have matched the in-game description. Similar names are not proof of identical effects. Check the target, activation condition, duration, resource cost and any stated limitation. If the translated recommendation depends on one ambiguous word, stop and resolve that word before spending resources. Our glossary gives ordinary terminology and class-name mappings; it does not claim every live item name. Separate portable technique from patch-specific numbers A habit such as recording why a pull failed can transfer well across regions. A precise cooldown alignment or damage threshold depends on current values and needs rechecking. Mark the parts of a guide you can practise without investment and try those first. Leave a gear purchase or irreversible choice until the relevant mechanic is confirmed in your client. This preserves the useful idea without importing an unverified budget. Run a small A/B check Keep equipment and encounter conditions as similar as possible. Try your existing approach several times, then change only the proposed mechanic. Record completion, avoidable mistakes and whether the change felt repeatable. A single lucky run cannot establish a better build. If damage measurements are unavailable or inconsistent, say so and judge only what you can observe reliably. Do not turn a personal impression into a universal DPS ranking. Credit the original and record the gap When sharing your conclusion, link the original creator, include the date you tested, and explain exactly what matched or differed. Summarise the useful lesson in your own words rather than republishing the full guide. If the global implementation is unknown, label it unverified. That small piece of missing context is often more valuable to the next reader than another confident tier label.

title: A calmer first group dungeon
description: Prepare a role, a clear pull plan and a useful way to learn after a wipe.
keywords: Prepare for the encounter you actually selected Read the current entry requirements and description inside the game. Do not use a party size or reward table copied from an older regional announcement. Before entering, tell the group if this is your first attempt and ask which mechanics require a specific assignment. Learning groups work better when expectations are explicit; a speed-clear listing may not be the right place for a first look. Give each person one clear priority Discuss who controls the pull, what the support players need from the group, and whether anyone has an assigned mechanic. A class name alone does not settle those responsibilities. If you are dealing damage, identify where you can stand without making support or movement harder. If you are supporting, position for visibility and safety before trying to rescue every avoidable mistake. Use the first pull to read the fight Watch for a repeated cue, then connect it to the consequence. Identify which movement was necessary and which was panic. Do not invent a boss rule from a single coincidence: ask the party or compare the next occurrence. When a mechanic is not understood, surviving long enough to see it again can teach more than forcing an ambitious damage sequence. This is a learning method, not a substitute for a verified boss guide. Review a wipe without a blame spiral Name the earliest observable problem, not just the final death. Was someone out of position before the dangerous sequence? Was an assignment unclear? Did the group attempt too much at once? Pick one adjustment for the next pull and leave everything else stable. Changing every skill, position and assignment together makes it difficult to learn which change mattered. Take home a reusable note Save the encounter name, region, difficulty, date and one concrete lesson. Separate an observed mechanic from something a teammate guessed. A note such as “move earlier when the cue appears” is useful only when you also know which cue. Over several sessions, your own small collection of reproducible observations becomes more valuable than an unfiltered list of tips.

title: Before your next upgrade: find the real bottleneck
description: A spending decision framework that begins with the encounter you want to clear.
keywords: Name the outcome before choosing an item “Get stronger” is too vague to compare purchases. Use an observable goal: survive a known sequence, meet a displayed entry requirement, or finish an encounter more consistently. If you cannot explain how a purchase helps that goal, postpone it. The purpose of this method is to avoid spending on a number that looks impressive but does not solve your current problem. Check execution before paying for power Look at several recent attempts. If most failures come from the same missed mechanic, practise that mechanic before assuming you need better equipment. If you execute consistently but still miss a clear requirement, an upgrade may be relevant. Keep those diagnoses separate. A damage increase cannot be assumed to compensate for an instant-failure condition or an uncompleted assignment. Read the full cost in the current client Include every displayed currency and material in your comparison, and read any binding, expiry or transfer restrictions. Check whether failure changes the cost before repeating an attempt. This guide supplies no enhancement probability, pity rule or guaranteed upgrade path: those need a current, region-specific source. A copied spreadsheet with the wrong assumptions can be more expensive than no spreadsheet. Choose a stopping rule in advance Set a resource budget before starting and keep enough for the activities you still want to play. Decide what you will do if the result is not what you hoped: wait, practise, gather more information or choose a different objective. Past spending is not evidence that the next attempt is worthwhile. Do not let a guide, a timer or another player’s equipment set your personal spending limit. Recheck the result against the original goal After changing equipment, repeat the same relevant activity and record what improved. If your original problem remains, diagnose it again rather than automatically purchasing the next upgrade. Keep a short record of the decision, expected benefit and observed result. Even a modest upgrade becomes a useful lesson when you can explain why it helped.

title: Why one PvP tier list cannot answer every question
description: Separate duel comfort, group responsibility and the conditions behind a PvP claim.
keywords: Define the fight before comparing classes A duel asks whether you can respond to one opponent. A group fight adds target selection, support, positioning and coordination. A larger fight changes visibility and the cost of overextending. None of these automatically predicts the others. When a tier list says “best at PvP”, look for the activity, region, patch and equipment assumptions before accepting the label. Evaluate decisions you can repeat Notice whether you identify a favourable engagement, keep an escape route and recognise when support is unavailable. Those decisions are useful to review even when you cannot measure damage reliably. A highlight can show a possibility; it does not show how often the player failed before recording it. Look for several comparable attempts, including losses. Keep the conditions visible Equipment differences, familiarity with an opponent, network conditions and party coordination can change the outcome. Do not assign the entire result to class balance. If you compare two approaches, keep as many conditions stable as possible and say what you could not control. A limited observation with clear conditions is more useful than a universal claim without them. Use a one-question practice session Choose one question for a short session: am I engaging too early, losing track of support, or staying after the favourable window closes? Review that question after each attempt. Once the behaviour is repeatable, move on to another. The goal is to learn which playstyle suits you and what you can improve, not to produce an invented numeric skill rating.

keywords: 선택한 던전의 조건을 읽으세요 게임 안에서 현재 입장 조건과 설명을 읽으세요. 예전 지역 공지에 있던 인원수나 보상표를 그대로 가져오지 마세요. 첫 도전이라면 미리 알리고 담당자를 정해야 하는 기믹이 있는지 물어보세요. 기대하는 목표를 공유한 파티가 배우기 좋습니다. 빠른 클리어를 원하는 모집은 첫 관찰에 맞지 않을 수 있습니다. 각자의 첫 우선순위를 정하세요 누가 전투를 시작하는지, 지원 역할이 파티에 바라는 점은 무엇인지, 특정 기믹 담당자가 있는지 확인하세요. 직업명만으로 모든 역할이 정해지는 것은 아닙니다. 공격 역할은 지원과 이동을 방해하지 않는 위치를 찾으세요. 지원 역할은 모든 실수를 수습하려 하기 전에 시야와 자신의 안전을 확보하세요. 첫 전투는 패턴을 읽는 시간 반복되는 신호를 보고 그 뒤의 결과와 연결하세요. 꼭 필요했던 이동과 당황해서 했던 이동을 구분해보세요. 한 번 우연히 일어난 일로 보스 규칙을 만들지 말고 파티에 묻거나 다음 상황과 비교하세요. 이해하지 못한 패턴이 있다면 무리한 공격보다 다시 볼 때까지 생존하는 편이 도움이 됩니다. 이 방법은 학습 과정이며 검증된 보스별 공략을 대신하지 않습니다. 실패 후 하나만 바꾸세요 마지막 사망 장면보다 처음 관찰된 문제를 찾으세요. 위험한 패턴 전에 위치가 어긋났는지, 담당이 불분명했는지, 한 번에 너무 많은 것을 하려 했는지 살펴보세요. 다음 전투에서는 한 가지만 바꾸고 다른 조건은 유지하세요. 기술과 위치와 담당을 모두 바꾸면 무엇이 효과가 있었는지 알기 어렵습니다. 다음에도 쓸 수 있는 메모 던전 이름, 지역, 난도, 날짜, 구체적인 교훈 하나를 남기세요. 직접 확인한 패턴과 파티원이 추측한 내용을 구분하세요. 신호가 나오면 빨리 움직이라는 메모는 어떤 신호인지 함께 적어야 쓸 수 있습니다. 재현 가능한 관찰을 조금씩 모으면 정리하지 않은 팁 목록보다 유용해집니다.

title: 다음 강화 전에, 무엇이 막히는지 확인하세요
description: 깨고 싶은 콘텐츠에서 출발하는 재화 사용 판단법.
keywords: 아이템보다 목표부터 정하세요 강해지고 싶다는 목표만으로는 구매를 비교하기 어렵습니다. 특정 패턴 생존, 화면에 표시된 입장 조건 충족, 더 안정적인 클리어처럼 관찰 가능한 목표를 정하세요. 구매가 그 목표에 어떻게 도움이 되는지 설명할 수 없다면 미뤄도 됩니다. 멋져 보이는 수치를 올리는 것과 지금의 문제를 푸는 것은 다를 수 있습니다. 투자 전에 전투 과정을 점검 최근 시도를 여러 번 돌아보세요. 같은 기믹 실수로 실패한다면 장비보다 해당 패턴을 먼저 연습하세요. 동작은 안정적이지만 명확한 조건을 계속 충족하지 못한다면 투자가 도움이 될 수 있습니다. 두 상황을 나누어 판단하세요. 피해량이 높아지면 모든 실패 조건이나 담당 누락을 해결한다고 가정할 수는 없습니다. 현재 화면의 전체 비용을 확인 표시된 재화와 재료를 모두 포함해 비교하고 귀속, 기간, 이전 제한을 읽으세요. 반복 시도 전에 실패가 비용에 어떤 영향을 주는지도 확인하세요. 이 글은 강화 확률, 천장 규칙, 확정 성장 경로를 제공하지 않습니다. 그런 수치는 현재 지역에 맞는 출처가 필요합니다. 전제가 틀린 계산표를 그대로 쓰면 오히려 손해를 볼 수 있습니다. 멈출 기준을 미리 정하세요 시작 전에 쓸 재료의 범위를 정하고 계속 즐길 활동에 필요한 여유를 남기세요. 원하는 결과가 나오지 않으면 기다릴지, 연습할지, 정보를 더 찾을지, 목표를 바꿀지 미리 정하세요. 이미 쓴 비용이 다음 시도의 가치를 증명하지는 않습니다. 공략, 남은 시간 표시, 다른 사람의 장비가 자신의 지출 한도를 결정하도록 두지 마세요. 처음 목표로 돌아가 확인 장비를 바꾼 뒤 같은 활동을 해보고 무엇이 나아졌는지 기록하세요. 원래 문제가 남아 있다면 다음 장비를 바로 사기보다 원인을 다시 살펴보세요. 선택, 기대한 효과, 실제 결과를 짧게 남겨두세요. 작은 성장이라도 왜 도움이 됐는지 설명할 수 있으면 다음 판단에 쓸 경험이 됩니다.

title: PvP 티어표 하나로 판단하기 어려운 이유
description: 1대1 조작감, 파티 역할, 평가 조건을 나눠 보는 방법.
keywords: 어떤 싸움인지 먼저 정하세요 결투는 한 명의 상대에 대응하는 능력을 봅니다. 파티 전투에는 대상 선택, 지원, 위치, 협력이 더해집니다. 규모가 커지면 시야와 무리한 진입의 위험도 달라집니다. 하나의 결과가 나머지를 자동으로 예측하지 않습니다. PvP 최강이라는 표현을 보면 콘텐츠, 지역, 패치, 장비 조건부터 확인하세요. 반복할 수 있는 판단을 보세요 유리한 싸움을 고르는지, 퇴로를 남기는지, 지원받을 수 없는 순간을 알아차리는지 보세요. 이런 판단은 피해량 측정이 어려워도 점검할 수 있습니다. 하이라이트는 가능한 장면을 보여주지만 그 전에 얼마나 실패했는지는 알려주지 않습니다. 패배를 포함한 비슷한 조건의 여러 시도를 살펴보세요. 조건을 숨기지 마세요 장비 차이, 상대에 대한 익숙함, 연결 상태, 파티 협력이 결과를 바꿀 수 있습니다. 결과 전체를 직업 밸런스의 효과로 돌리지 마세요. 두 방법을 비교할 때는 가능한 조건을 유지하고 통제하지 못한 부분을 밝히세요. 조건이 분명한 제한적 관찰이 조건 없는 일반화보다 유용합니다. 한 번에 질문 하나만 연습 짧은 시간 동안 질문 하나를 정하세요. 너무 빨리 진입하는지, 지원 위치를 놓치는지, 유리한 시간이 끝나도 남아 있는지 중 하나면 됩니다. 매 시도 후 그 질문을 돌아보세요. 동작이 안정되면 다른 질문으로 옮기세요. 자신에게 맞는 스타일과 개선할 행동을 찾는 과정이지 근거 없는 실력 점수를 만드는 과정은 아닙니다.
